content.text:
Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Repo indkhan/Moneo. Fix GitHub issue #272 (read it with `gh issue view 272`, and AGENTS.md, especially "Database changes", "Desktop app" and "Tests"): `ingest_import_batch` ends with `recount_import_progress(p_import_id)`, which recounts the whole import after every 250-row batch (O(N²)). Choose the simplest correct option: either recount only the batch's own rows and add the delta, or keep running totals updated by the row writes; in both cases keep a final full recount in `finish_import_run` as the check. The progress counts must stay exactly correct after every batch, including re-imports, duplicates/matched rows, review rows, rejected rows and undo (read `recount_import_progress` and every place that changes those counts). Concurrency: two batches of the same import must not lose updates (row lock on the import, or atomic `update ... set x = x + delta`).

Steps:
1. Create branch `t3/issue-272-import-recount` from origin/main. Reproduce with `supabase/tests/import-batch-throughput.mjs` on moneo-qa (rollback-only, synthetic) and record the blocks-per-row numbers at 1,000 and 10,000 rows.
2. Add a new ordered migration in `supabase/migrations/` with a prefix later than the newest file on main. Patch the functions with `create or replace` copied from their CURRENT definitions (check the latest migration that defines each one, or `pg_get_functiondef` on QA), changing only what this needs. It must run on the owner's existing database and in the desktop bundle (no extensions it lacks). Keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned if any column changes, and run `npm run db:types`.
3. Add or extend a SQL regression in `supabase/tests/` (see `supabase/tests/README.md`) that checks the counts after each batch equal a full recount, including a duplicate/matched case and a review case.
4. Tighten the throughput script's assertion to about 1.2× as the issue says, and put before/after numbers in the PR body.
5. If you apply your migration to moneo-qa to test, revert it afterwards (restore the previous function definitions and delete its `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` row), because other agents share that database.

Rules: run `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:db` and `npm run build` yourself and quote their last lines. Tests use only the moneo-qa test backend; never the owner's backend (.env, Docker project `moneo`, port 3000). Never run `qa:reset` or `docker compose -p moneo-qa down`. Never kill a process you didn't start (verify by PID). Don't end your turn while a command is still running. No comments in TypeScript code. Commits end with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>". Before opening the PR, merge origin/main again. Open the PR (body ends with "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)"), never merge it. Final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>.

Fixes #272.

`ingest_import_batch` recounted every source row of the import after each 250-row batch (O(N²/250)). It now reads the import's totals under the import lock (held by `read_import_stage`), counts only its own 250-row window before and after, and writes `totals − before + after`. `record_import_exclusion` no longer recounts either; it adds one to `rejected_rows` when it inserts a new rejected row. `finish_import_run`, undo and review corrections still do the full `recount_import_progress`, which stays the check. Measured with `supabase/tests/import-batch-throughput.mjs` on moneo-qa (rollback-only, synthetic), buffer blocks per row:

| rows | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |

| 10,000 | 280 | 147 |
| ratio | 1.9× | 1.08× |

The script now asserts at most 1.2× (was 3×).

New SQL regression `supabase/tests/import-batch-progress.sql`: a 501-row import in three batches with a matched row (re-import against an earlier import), review rows, a new row with classification review, and exclusions in batch 1 and batch 3. After each batch the counts must equal a full recount, and retrying the batch must not change them. Breaking the delta for `review_rows` or `classification_review_rows` makes it fail.

content.text:
PR #301 is open and not merged. `npm run test:db` has two failures in `lib/ai/data-query.live.test.ts`; the other 15 of 17 tests pass.

- **Fix:** each batch now counts only its own 250-row window before and after, and writes `totals − before + after`. The totals are read under the import lock, so two batches of the same import can't lose updates. `record_import_exclusion` now adds one to `rejected_rows` instead of recounting. `finish_import_run`, undo and review corrections still do the full recount, so it remains the check.
- **Migration:** `202611180001_import_batch_progress_delta.sql` adds one helper function and replaces two functions with `create or replace`. No columns change, and it uses nothing the desktop bundle lacks. I ran `npm run db:types`, which added the new helper to `lib/database.types.ts`.
- **Numbers:** buffer blocks per row from the throughput script:

| rows | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1,000 | 147 | 136 |
| 10,000 | 280 | 147 |

  The ratio at 10,000 vs 1,000 rows went from 1.9× to 1.08×. The script now asserts at most 1.2× (was 3×).
- **New regression:** `supabase/tests/import-batch-progress.sql` ingests 501 rows in three batches. It includes a matched re-import row, review rows, a classification-review row and exclusions in batches 1 and 3. After each batch the counts must equal a full recount, and retrying the batch must not change them. Breaking the delta for `review_rows` or `classification_review_rows` makes it fail.
- **Checks:**
  - `npm test`: 1884 passed, 17 skipped.
  - `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build`: clean.
  - `node supabase/tests/migrations.mjs`: 145 migrations and 64 SQL regressions pass.
- **`test:db` failures:** both are `data-query.live.test.ts`. The moneo-qa `moneo_query` schema has no views, which this change doesn't touch.
- **QA database:** I didn't apply my migration to moneo-qa, so nothing needed reverting. Setting up the worktree applied one existing migration from main there.
